s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk in a patient with a history of systemic sclerosis
salient_findings: Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
Nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles on lesional punch biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis
Patient has a history of heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
Patient is receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Rash is pruritic and has been present for 3 months
Patient denied any known preceding triggers or trauma to the area of the rash
Review of systems was negative for any new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Complete blood cell count with differential was unremarkable
Tissue cultures obtained by punch biopsy were negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus

shortlist.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and is presenting with a pruritic rash, which is consistent with nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Lesional punch biopsy specimens showed nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers, which is consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis

shortlist.label: Scleromyxedema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and is presenting with firm, red-brown plaques, which is consistent with scleromyxedema

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and is presenting with a pruritic rash, which is consistent with morphea

shortlist.label: Chronic scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and is presenting with a pruritic rash, which is consistent with chronic scleroderma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, along with the histopathological findings of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers and homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles, is consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis. The absence of skin tightening in the affected areas and the lack of other systemic symptoms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
rejected.why: The patient's kidney function is not mentioned as being impaired, which is a typical prerequisite for nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

rejected.label: Scleromyxedema
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic mucin deposition and lichenoid papules seen in scleromyxedema

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: The patient's lesions are described as firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, which is not typical of morphea, and the histopathological findings do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Chronic scleroderma
rejected.why: The patient already has a history of systemic sclerosis, but the current presentation is distinct from typical chronic scleroderma, with a lack of skin tightening and other characteristic features
